summary: Provenance-backed, privacy-safe, version-aware model and searchable source corpus for roughly 20 years of RTEC HR process documentation.
current_priorities: Continue the resumable PC filesystem reconciliation in audits/filesystem-reconciliation/RECONCILIATION_STATUS.md; metadata/hash discovery and deterministic extraction of all 15,441 candidates are complete. Cache-only OCR is operational (12 complete, 5 restricted samples, 6,392 pending) with image-size and thread limits. Local normalized-text duplicates are grouped (2,525 groups). Reconciliation separates 30 explicit source/file hash matches from 467 unverified generic/content hash matches. Filename-only HR GUI routing hints classify 173 restricted documents; continue OCR, review duplicate/version chains, then reconcile safe candidates before Knowledge Engine ingestion. R: remains excluded.

Import the six distinct unindexed local PST candidates recorded in projects/rtec-hr-process-model/checkpoints/pst-archive-source-inventory.json after coordinating with the active read-only email-review pass; deduplicate at message level and preserve restricted content only in the local mail index.
Continue the FY2017 grant scan ingestion in bounded, restart-safe section batches; do not attempt monolithic OCR of all 1,021 pages.
Use grant checklists as the section map and deduplicate repeated assurances/certifications against the !Compliance archive before transcribing copies.
Promote the FY2017-era 2015–2018 AAP, September 2016 Title VI/LEP plan, 2016 EEO certification material, ADA complaint process and related forms as canonical historical compliance sources.
Build version chains from the FY2017-era compliance sources through later/current AAP, EEO and Title VI/LEP versions.
Continue ingesting the broader historical RTEC HR document base in small committed batches.

Preserve safe manuals, policies, procedures, templates, training/reference sources, grant binders and organizational materials in full searchable form while keeping restricted person-level case data out of GitHub.

Use the correspondence archive to reconcile current discipline, attendance/leave, administrative approval, CSR escalation, employee-evaluation and employee-guidance workflows against newer authoritative sources.
Continue clause-level review of the preserved 2017 and draft1 2019 driver handbooks; confirm blank receipt layouts and determine whether either version was approved or superseded.
Locate and evaluate the July 2021 proposed attendance-policy memo; resolve adoption date and treatment of existing points against the distinct July PDF and tracked-change DOCX handbook copies.
Resolve the current FMLA administrator and leave workflow; the 2018 archive only records a vendor inquiry.
constraints: GitHub stores derived sanitized process knowledge, not live employee/applicant records or raw OCR.
Do not generalize employee-specific case facts into global process rules.
Uncertain claims remain candidates until corroborated or user-confirmed.
Preserve source provenance and document-version context for every promoted rule.
HR-GUI PROJECT_GUIDE.md privacy rules remain authoritative for scanner development.
Do not assume an older source is current; determine effective period and supersession before relying on it operationally.

corpus_scope.temporal_assumption: Historical by default until effective period/currentness is established.
corpus_scope.preservation_rule: Retain obsolete and superseded process sources for chronology and legacy-reference purposes.

reference_form_context.full_source_rule: When a safe original reference artifact is available, preserve it in full or by a lossless repository-safe representation and link it to the existing catalog entry.
reference_form_context.authority_rule: Form presence is contextual evidence, not automatic current policy authority.

job_description_context.integrity_status: all 14 searchable source-group mirrors verified byte-for-byte against the extracted local corpus using Git blob hashes
job_description_context.temporal_rule: Historical/unknown by default until current approved versions and effective dates are established.
job_description_context.privacy_rule: Employee-specific temporary light-duty descriptions are restricted metadata-only and excluded from reusable role knowledge.

correspondence_context.privacy_rule: Employee-level disciplinary, medical, incident, schedule, leave-case, and participant-list content remains restricted. Exhaustive analysis promotes only reusable structure, policy/process evidence, aggregate data-quality findings and unresolved questions.
notable_findings: Historical discipline registers became mixed discipline-plus-vehicle-incident ledgers from 2016-2017 onward.
AAP derivatives are versioned transformations, not reliable identical copies; one 2016-2017 variant systematically recodes EEO categories.
Fiscal register migration requires schema detection, alias normalization and stable source-row identities; person/date/reason is not a safe dedupe key.
Old 9/10-point attendance thresholds are superseded by the current 2025 six-point system.
Historical medical/attendance evidence handling supports restricted evidence separation from ordinary attendance records.
All 33 individual warning/counseling files have been mapped to generalized knowledge themes.
correspondence_context.completion_boundary: No supplied artifact remains without an explicit analysis disposition. Further progress on unresolved current-state questions requires newer/authoritative sources rather than rereading this archive.
correspondence_context.exhaustion_boundary: All 95 supplied artifacts have been structurally/content-analyzed to the privacy-safe boundary and mapped to durable knowledge. Remaining open questions require newer or more authoritative sources rather than further rereading of this archive.
